Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — deployment mode needs

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary:
- Current setup: you’re calling OpenAI’s hosted API for general workloads and maintaining an internal legacy GPU cluster for higher-sensitivity workloads.
- Primary goals: reduce per-token cost for high-volume inference, improve 99th percentile latency for customer-facing features, and ensure PHI/PII stays in your controlled environment.

Open questions we flagged:
- Monthly token/embedding volume (approx), and peak RPS during business hours
- Which model families you want supported on day one (OpenAI-equivalent vs custom fine-tuned models)
- Any strict data residency / SOC2 / HIPAA requirements beyond what we discussed

Deployment options that fit your needs (high level):
1) Hosted API — fastest time-to-value, best for non-sensitive workloads and bursty traffic
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools (SLA-backed) for predictable latency and throughput; good if you want isolated capacity without managing infra
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — required for regulated PHI workflows or full network isolation; we support an on-prem package if needed

Recommended next steps:
1) Share a short answers sheet to the security questions attached (security-questions.xlsx) — helps us scope Private vs Dedicated requirements
2) I’m attaching a short POC proposal (POC-proposal.pdf) with a proposed scope for a Dedicated POC that includes a migration plan from OpenAI tokens and integration guidance for your legacy cluster
3) Technical kickoff with Michael (SE) — he’ll draft a migration plan and estimate effort once we have volumes and SLOs

If you can reply with token volumes (rough ballpark is fine) and whether you need VPC/on-prem for all workloads or just a subset, we’ll put together a tailored proposal and tentative timeline.

Proposed scheduling: 30-min migration scoping call next week — I have Tue/Wed 10–12 PT open.

Thanks,

—

- Peak: around 400 RPS during US business hours for the customer chat flows.

Hey Alex / Marissa —

Thanks for the details, Alex — that volume and peak RPS align with a couple of typical patterns we see. A few technical notes from the SE side: 

- Dedicated is a solid first step for latency-sensitive customer chat flows; we can size reserved GPU pools to give you consistent 99th pctl latency targets.
- For PHI: Private VPC or on-prem are both supported. Private VPC with customer-managed peering and KMS integration will typically be faster to stand up than a full on-prem install. If you need air-gapped processing of raw PHI, on-prem is the route.
- Migration approach (high level):
  1) Start with dual-write for a 2-week shadow period (traffic routed to OpenAI + Redwood Dedicated) to compare latency/cost and validate parity
  2) Run a rolling cutover by route (chat first, then batch)
  3) Use our KV/prefix caching to preserve cost on common prompts and reduce token spend for the chat paths
- Questions that change sizing and timeline: model sequence length distributions, tokenization mix (avg tokens per request), expected concurrency for batch jobs, and whether you want model quantization on day one.

I attached a short migration plan draft (migration-plan-draft.md) that outlines the cutover steps and required checkpoints (security review, perf validation, canary). Once we confirm volumes and SLOs we’ll produce an estimate for Dedicated sizing and cost delta vs Hosted.

Happy to take the scoping call Wed 10am PT — I’ll bring latency numbers from similar POCs and a recommended Dedicated config.

—
